messages:
Aisha: Quick thread — we need to standardize the internal incident comms templates. Not just public status page copy, but the internal playbook snippets we post in on-call handoffs and incident channels. Tone, placeholders, and a couple of standard sections (impact, mitigation, next steps).

Tom: +1. Last pager we had a lot of back-and-forth about what to put in the first 10m update. Folks were uncertain about what counts as 'customer impact'.

Carlos: Agree. We should have two micro-templates: 'initial triage' (first 5-10m) and 'customer-facing draft' (if P1/P2 with customer impact). Keep internal updates more operational.

IncidentBot: :rotating_light: paging @oncall — Incident created: INC-2026-0421. Severity: P2. Summary: increased 5xx on text-generation endpoint.

Aisha: Adding a proposed internal template (short). Use this in incident channels and for handoffs. Please comment inline.

Marta: Nice. Can we add a tiny checklist at the top for handoffs? Eg: "handoff: yes/no, assignee, ETA" — saves repeating.

Aisha: Good idea. Updated. Here are two templates (pasteable snippets):

```
Internal — initial (5–10m)
- Handoff: [yes/no], Assignee: [name]
- What happened: one-line summary (user-facing phrasing)
- Impact: systems/customers impacted, % requests failing or latency delta
- Mitigation in progress: [what we're trying now]
- Next steps / owner: [who will do what in next 15m]
- Notify customers? [yes/no] (only if confirmed customer impact)

Internal — incident update (post-triage)
- Incident ID: [INC-YYYY-NNNN]
- Severity: [P1/P2/P3]
- Root cause hypothesis: [short]
- Scope & impact: [affected endpoints, regions, customers]*
- Actions taken: [list]
- Current status: [investigating/mitigating/partial service restored/resolved]
- ETA for next update: [time or conditions]
- Communication owner: [name]
```

Aisha: And a customer-facing status page / email draft for ops to copy: keep empathetic, non-technical, and include workaround if available.

```
Customer-facing (short)
- What happened: We experienced an issue affecting text generation requests which caused some requests to fail or timeout.
- Impact: A subset of customers in [region] may have seen increased errors or delays between [time window].
- What we're doing: Our engineers have identified the cause and are applying mitigations to restore normal service.
- Workaround: If you rely on synchronous generation, try increasing client-side timeouts or retrying once after 5s.
- Next update: we will post another status at [ETA] or when service is stable.
- Contact: [support@redwood.ai] (for high-impact customers request dedicated channel).
```

Tom: Love the structure. Quick tone pointers:
- Use active voice but avoid certainty if we don't have root cause. Eg "we are investigating" not "root cause is X".
- No blame or vendor names in customer copy.
- Short bullets — ops people appreciate scanability.

Elena: From CS: add a placeholder for 'customers to proactively contact' (like key accounts we should DM). Also add an escalation line: "If customer X asks, route to CS Pager."

Carlos: On handoffs: make it explicit when to do a formal handoff vs quick update. Suggest: if incident >30m or severity escalates, do a handoff with 1:1 summary and set active owner.

Marta: Also propose a tiny library of one-liner tones for start-of-incident lines so people don't reinvent language. Examples:
- blunt: "We are investigating increased error rate on generation endpoint."
- empathetic: "We're aware some customers are seeing failed requests — sorry for the disruption."
- internal ops: "High 5xx rate detected; triage in progress."

Aisha: These are gold. I want a short doc page with examples + a copy-paste button that ops can use when escalating to customers or updating the status page. I'll put the canonical snippets in the playbook repo.

Tom: One more: add a tiny 'what not to say' list: no speculative RCs, no SLA legal phrasing, no promises on ETA unless validated.

Marta: I'll draft the doc and add the snippets as code blocks and a small decision tree: "Is it customer-impacting? -> Yes -> use customer template and notify CS; No -> internal updates only."

IncidentBot: :pushpin: Reminder: incident channel naming convention — use #inc-INC-YYYY-NNNN during active incident.

Aisha: Next steps: Marta to draft PR for playbook + snippets, Carlos to propose handoff timing rules, Elena to provide list of high-touch customers for DM templates. I'll review and we ship by EOD tomorrow.

Elena: I can get that list today and add suggested templates for DMs.

Carlos: Will draft handoff rules now.

Marta: Draft PR opened: https://git.internal.redwood/repo/playbook/pull/42 — please review.

Tom: Reviewed and left small wording suggestions. Also added a kebab-case label for the snippet filenames (inc-templates/internal.md).

Aisha: Thanks team. Final ask — when posting internal updates during incident, paste the short 'Internal — initial' block at the top so the channel is uniform. We'll enforce that in postmortems if not followed. :thumbsup:
